name: Annual operating budget for one business unit
summary: Once a year each business unit builds its operating budget for the next year: revenue, costs, headcount and capital. Corporate FP&A issues targets and templates, the unit's analyst preloads a spreadsheet model, cost centre managers and the sales director fill in their parts, and the analyst consolidates them for the finance manager and general manager to challenge. The unit submits to corporate, where executives usually set new targets for at least one revision round before the board approves the company budget. Most of the elapsed time is waiting for managers' submissions, review meetings and board dates, and the many spreadsheet versions cause errors and rework.

baseline.org_archetype: One business unit (about $200 million revenue, 500 to 700 employees, about ten cost centres) of a US mid-size company with a calendar fiscal year, spreadsheet templates and a corporate planning tool.
baseline.notes: Incremental budgeting from last year's base with top-down targets, the most common approach; zero-based budgeting would add much more manager time.

unit_of_work: one business unit's annual operating budget
trigger: Corporate FP&A issues the budget calendar, targets and templates, usually in early autumn for a calendar year.
end_state: The board has approved the company budget and this unit's budget is loaded by month in the ERP and communicated to its managers.

volume.seasonality: Once a year, concentrated from about September to December for a calendar fiscal year.

evidence.note: One budget per business unit per year by definition.

triggered_by.from: Corporate FP&A (strategic plan and annual planning calendar)

systems.name: Spreadsheet budget model and cost centre templates
ERP general ledger (actuals and loaded budget)
HR information system (headcount roster and pay)

steps.name: Issue budget calendar, targets and templates
steps.description: Corporate FP&A sends each business unit the budget calendar, top-down revenue and profit targets, planning assumptions such as inflation, merit increase and benefit rates, the corporate allocations, and the templates to complete.

error.defect_description: Assumption or template error that every business unit copies

control.basis: Budget policy and procedures issued by corporate FP&A (APQC PCF 9.1.1.1 develop and maintain budget policies and procedures)

evidence.note: Milestone calendar and written policies (acctools_planning); PCF 9.1.1.1. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Build the business unit model and preload actuals
steps.description: The business unit financial analyst builds the unit's budget workbook, loads year-to-date actuals and the run-rate forecast from the ERP, pulls the headcount roster, and preloads each cost centre template with history adjusted for inflation so managers only change what is different.

error.defect_description: Link or formula error in the preloaded templates

evidence.note: Preloading a model from historical results (acctools_planning); incremental budgeting from last year's base (acca_budget). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Hold the business unit kick-off and set assumptions
steps.description: The general manager meets the finance manager, sales director and department heads to walk through the targets, agree the unit's priorities and key assumptions such as volume growth and new hires, and hand out the templates and deadline.

evidence.note: Kickoff training reduces stakeholder questions (cfo_budget). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Prepare cost centre expense and headcount submissions
steps.description: About ten cost centre managers update their templates with planned headcount and hires, travel, contractors, supplies and projects, and write short justifications for increases. Most work on it close to the submission deadline about two weeks after kick-off.

error.defect_description: Overwritten formulas, wrong version of the template, or padded estimates

evidence.note: Managers adjust their sections (acctools_planning); participative budgeting and padding incentives (acctools_master); budgetary slack (acca_budget); a zero-based budget would take managers much longer (wiki_zbb). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Prepare revenue and volume forecast
steps.description: The sales director and account managers build the revenue budget by customer or product line from the CRM pipeline, expected price changes and volume trends, and send it to the analyst.

error.defect_description: Revenue set low to make targets easier to beat

evidence.note: Sales budget is the first component of the master budget; targets tied to pay encourage underestimated sales (acctools_master). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Provide headcount and compensation data
steps.description: The HR compensation analyst validates the unit's headcount roster, applies merit increase, bonus and benefit rates to each position, and prices the requested new hires, then sends the file to the analyst.

error.defect_description: Vacant or transferred positions priced wrongly

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Prepare capital expenditure requests
steps.description: The operations or engineering manager lists planned equipment, facilities and IT projects with costs, timing and a short business case for each, ranked by priority, for review with the general manager.

control.basis: Capital expenditure policy: requests above a threshold need a business case and ranking before inclusion

next.condition: all submissions in by the deadline

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Chase late or incomplete submissions
steps.description: The analyst tracks which templates are missing or incomplete, emails and calls the managers, and escalates to the finance manager or general manager when deadlines slip.

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Consolidate submissions and compare with targets
steps.description: The analyst loads all templates into the business unit model, fixes broken formulas and version mix-ups, reconciles headcount to the HR file, and builds a summary comparing the draft with the targets, the current year forecast and prior year, highlighting the gap.

evidence.note: Returned segments aggregated into a master model (acctools_planning). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Business unit finance manager reviews the draft
steps.description: The finance manager reviews the consolidated draft for errors, unsupported increases and gaps to target, agrees questions to raise with managers, and decides whether it is ready for the general manager.

next.condition: send back to managers for fixes

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: General manager review and challenge session
steps.description: The general manager meets finance and each department head, challenges headcount additions and spending increases against the targets, and either approves the business unit submission or asks for cuts and changes.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: the business unit general manager approves the unit budget before submission

evidence.note: Several review iterations (acctools_master); median of five budget versions (cfo_budget). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Managers revise submissions
steps.description: Cost centre managers rework their templates to the requested cuts or corrections, often pushing back on cuts or moving costs between lines, and resend them.

error.defect_description: Revision made in an old version of the template

evidence.note: Back-and-forth negotiation produces multiple versions and waiting (cfo_budget). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Analyst updates the model and version log
steps.description: The analyst loads the revised templates, reruns the consolidation and gap summary, and records what changed between versions so reviewers can see the movement.

evidence.note: Strict version control recommended where there is no single version of the truth (cfo_budget). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Submit the business unit budget to corporate FP&A
steps.description: The analyst re-keys or uploads the approved budget into the corporate planning template or tool by line and month, attaches the commentary deck and capital list, and confirms the submission totals agree to the unit model.

error.defect_description: Upload or re-keying error between the unit model and the corporate tool

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Corporate FP&A consolidates and compares with company targets
steps.description: Once all business units have submitted, corporate FP&A consolidates them, adds corporate costs and allocations, compares the total with the company profit and cash targets, and prepares the gap analysis for the executive reviews.

error.defect_description: Allocation error moves cost to the wrong unit

evidence.note: Segments aggregated into a master model that senior management reviews (acctools_planning). The wait covers other units' submissions. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Executive challenge session
steps.description: The CFO and CEO review the business unit's budget with its general manager and finance manager, challenge revenue that looks low and costs that look high against the company target, and accept it or set new targets for a revision round.

control.basis: Executive review of business unit budgets before the company budget goes to the board

evidence.note: Senior management often requires changes, leading to repeated revisions (acctools_planning). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: General manager decides revisions to meet new targets
steps.description: The general manager and finance manager decide where to cut or what extra revenue to commit, usually by deferring hires, trimming discretionary spending or delaying capital projects, and agree the changes with department heads.

error.defect_description: Cuts placed on lines that will be spent anyway

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Analyst rebuilds the model and resubmits
steps.description: The analyst applies the agreed revisions, updates the headcount and capital schedules and the commentary, and resubmits to corporate FP&A in the planning tool.

error.defect_description: Revision not carried through to every schedule

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Corporate FP&A reviews the revised submission
steps.description: Corporate FP&A checks that the revised submission closes the agreed gap, ties out to the planning tool and is consistent with other units, and either accepts it or asks for another round.

evidence.note: Iterations and waiting dominate the budget cycle (cfo_budget). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Executive team finalises the company budget
steps.description: The CFO and CEO sign off the consolidated company budget, including this unit, and prepare the board materials with the budget, key assumptions and risks.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: CEO and CFO approve the company operating budget for board submission

evidence.note: Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Board approves the annual budget
steps.description: At its next scheduled meeting the board reviews the company budget and approves it, occasionally asking for changes. This unit's share of board time is small, but the case waits for the meeting date.

control.basis: Corporate governance: the board approves the annual operating budget under its charter or bylaws

evidence.note: Board signs off once all parties accept the model (acctools_planning). Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Load the approved budget into the ERP and phase it by month
steps.description: The analyst spreads the approved annual figures by month using seasonality and hiring dates, loads them by cost centre and account into the ERP or planning tool for budget-versus-actual reporting, and checks the loaded totals.

error.defect_description: Phasing or load error that distorts monthly variances

evidence.note: Budget loaded into accounting software for budget-versus-actual reporting. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

steps.name: Communicate the final budget to managers
steps.description: The finance manager sends each cost centre manager their final budget, headcount and capital approvals, explains changes from their submission, and confirms the targets they will be measured against.

evidence.note: PCF 9.1.1.3 operationalise and implement plans to achieve budget. Touch and wait ranges and branch shares are author estimates for one business unit (about $200 million revenue, ten cost centres) of a mid-size US company budgeting in spreadsheets with an ERP in 2019 to 2022.

exceptions.name: Late or incomplete submissions
exceptions.description: Some managers miss the deadline or send incomplete templates; the analyst chases and escalates.

exceptions.name: Business unit revision loop
exceptions.description: The finance manager or general manager sends the draft back for fixes or cuts; managers revise and the analyst updates the model before another review.

exceptions.name: Executive revision round
exceptions.description: Executives set new targets; the general manager decides cuts, the analyst rebuilds and corporate reviews again, sometimes twice.

exceptions.name: Board changes
exceptions.description: The board asks for changes, sending the unit back to a revision round.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from issuing budget objectives to a ready-to-use approved budget

evidence.note: Derived: APQC's top quarter finish in 28 days or less and are nearly twice as fast as the 75th percentile (about 56 days); the median is not published, so p50 is set between the two. p90 is an author estimate for slower organisations with board dates and several revision rounds.
Covers all budgeting and forecasting work, not only the annual budget.
Quarterly rolling forecast, a smaller exercise than the annual budget; useful as a lower bound.

pain_points.description: Most elapsed time is waiting: for managers to fill templates near the deadline, for review meetings on busy calendars, for other units to submit and for the board date.

evidence.note: APQC notes much of the cycle is waiting rather than working.

pain_points.description: Back-and-forth negotiation produces several budget versions; managers pad requests expecting cuts and executives cut expecting padding.

evidence.note: Median of five versions (cfo_budget); budgetary slack (acca_budget).

pain_points.description: Spreadsheet templates break, versions get mixed up and figures are re-keyed into the corporate tool, so analysts spend days on consolidation and checks.
Late or incomplete submissions need chasing and escalation.

evidence.note: Author's reading of common practice.

sources.title: 4 tips for a faster and more effective budgeting process: Metric of the Month (Perry D. Wiggins, citing APQC)
sources.supports: APQC data from nearly 6,000 organisations: cycle time to complete the annual budget, in calendar days from setting budget objectives to delivering a ready-to-use budget; the top quarter finish in 28 days or less, nearly twice as fast as organisations at the 75th percentile; a median of five budget versions from back-and-forth negotiation, with much of the cycle spent waiting rather than working; starting later, kickoff training and a single version of the truth shorten it.

sources.title: Measuring financial forecasting efficiency: Metric of the Month (citing APQC)
sources.supports: FTEs synthesising financial data to develop budgets and forecasts per $1 billion revenue: 25th percentile 1.9, median 3.4, 75th percentile 5.4 (all industries).

sources.title: 4 strategies for faster financial forecasting: Metric of the Month (citing APQC)
sources.supports: Cycle time to prepare a financial forecast (generally a quarterly rolling P&L forecast): median 11 days, high performers 8 days, nearly 3,900 companies.

sources.title: 9.0 Manage financial resources (APQC Process Classification Framework, cross-industry, reproduced)
sources.supports: APQC PCF 9.1.1 Perform planning, budgeting and forecasting: develop and maintain budget policies and procedures, prepare periodic budgets and plans, operationalise and implement plans, prepare periodic forecasts, perform variance analysis.

sources.title: Budgetary planning
sources.supports: Process: board sets strategic direction; milestone calendar; written policies and procedures; budget owner preloads a model from historical results; managers adjust their sections; segments aggregated into a master model that senior management reviews and often sends back for repeated revisions; board sign-off; budget loaded into accounting software for budget-versus-actual reporting.

sources.title: Master budget
sources.supports: Master budget components (sales, production, materials, labour, overhead, selling and administrative, cash, financing, budgeted statements); senior management reviews several iterations; participative budgeting; spreadsheets common in smaller organisations; tying targets to pay leads managers to underestimate sales and overstate expenses.

sources.title: Comparing budgeting techniques
sources.supports: Incremental budgeting starts from the current budget or actuals plus increments; it is quick, cheap and limits conflict but carries forward slack and encourages spend-it-or-lose-it; zero-based budgeting uses decision packages, ranking and allocation.

sources.title: Zero-based budgeting
sources.supports: Zero-based budgeting requires every expense to be justified each period through decision units, decision packages and ranking; it takes more time, effort and staff than budgeting from last year's base.

assumptions: General workflow for one business unit of about $200 million revenue in a US company of about 2,000 employees; one budget per year (cases_per_month = 1/12).
Loaded cost per hour = BLS May 2021 wage x 1.8 (benefits factor 1.43 from BLS ECEC December 2021, overhead factor 1.25 estimated).
Incremental budgeting from last year's base with top-down targets; zero-based budgeting would add decision packages and ranking and much more manager time (wiki_zbb).
Hands-on times for groups (cost centre managers, executives) are totals across the people involved for this unit.

The submission window (s04) is modelled as the wait before managers' work; revenue, headcount and capital inputs (s05 to s07) run in parallel with near-zero waits, but the simulator still adds their hands-on time to elapsed time.

The simulator reuses the same branch probabilities on every revision pass, so the number of rounds follows a geometric distribution; on average this gives about four versions (about 2.2 business unit drafts plus 0.7 executive revision rounds and the final), a little below the APQC median of five.
Stated FTE is averaged over the year; budget work is concentrated in about three months, when the analyst spends about half their time on it.
The APQC median cycle time is not published; the benchmark p50 of 42 days is set between the published top-quarter (28 days) and 75th-percentile (about 56 days) values.
Branch shares (late submissions, revision rounds, board changes) are author estimates.

The simulated median (about 58 days) is 1.4 times the derived benchmark of 42 days and sits just above the APQC 75th percentile of about 56 days. About 9 of those days are hands-on time that the simulator adds in sequence although much of it happens in parallel or inside the submission window.
